channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: Kallas Says Iranian Capacity To Target Gulf States 'Unsustainable'
item.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says she doubts Iran’s capacity to sustain its pace of attacks on countries across the Middle East given its decimated military following the 12-day war last year with Israel and the current US-Israeli campaign launched against it over the weekend.

item.title: The Administrator, The Wild Card, The Heir: The Clerics Vying For Iran's Top Job
item.description: Iran's Assembly of Experts is convening to pick the Islamic republic's next supreme leader after the death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in US-Israeli strikes. Here's a look at the leading contenders: Alireza Arafi, Hassan Khomeini, and Mojtaba Khamenei.

item.title: Exclusive: Kremlin Office Plants Prove Putin's Absence As Iran War Heats Up
item.description: On March 2-3, the Kremlin published videos showing him meeting with officials and indicated the footage was fresh. In fact, both meetings were recorded earlier, Systema, RFE/RL’s Russian investigative unit, has determined – the latest example of what has become a common practice for Putin’s office.

item.title: US Confirms Sinking Iranian Ship, Says Tehran Firing Fewer Missiles
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed a US submarine sank ‌an Iranian warship off the coast of Sri Lanka as military officials said Iran is firing fewer missiles at targets around the Gulf region due to its decimated capabilities to wage war.

item.title: Russia's 'Maximalist Demands' Cannot Be Met With 'Minimalist Response,' EU's Kallas Says
item.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the bloc may be open to direct talks with Moscow on trying to help settle the war in Ukraine but Moscow will have to temper its "maximalist" demands to pave the way for negotiations.

item.title: 'Devastation': Tehran Resident Describes Life Under Ongoing Missile Strikes
item.description: RFE/RL's Radio Farda spoke with a woman in Tehran who described life in the Iranian capital as it faces days of ongoing missile strikes. Her voice has been altered for security reasons. The US and Israel continue military operations against Iran, while Teheran retaliates with strikes.

item.title: Kremlin-Friendly Media Changing Their Story On Iran
item.description: Russia's state-sponsored media pundits have long praised Iran as a strategic partner and ally -- but faced with ongoing US-Israeli strikes on Iran, these outlets are arguing that Iran was never to be counted on. Some Russian commentators even seen celebrate the struggles of the Islamic republic.

item.title: In Bunkers And On Streets, Israelis Celebrate Purim Amid Repeated Missile Strikes
item.description: RFE/RL correspondent Ray Furlong was at Purim celebrations in Jerusalem as air attack sirens sounded. “It’s definitely scary,” said one reveler, as the party moved underground.

item.title: Israeli Purim Celebrations Defy Iranian Missiles
item.description: Israelis were celebrating Purim with singing, dancing, and costume parties on March 4. When the festivities in Jerusalem were interrupted by an air-raid alert, people headed for the shelters and kept partying there -- determined to maintain normal life amid war.

item.title: Attacks On Iran Continue As US Senate Blocks Bid To Limit Trump's War Authority
item.description: US and Israeli forces continued to strike against Iran, while the US Senate rejected a bid that would have limited President Donald Trump’s authority to continue military action against the Middle East country without congressional approval.
